comments.text_zh: 这里是 Microsoft Research 那篇臭名昭著的 Nagappan TDD 论文 [LINK]，这篇 infoq 文章也讨论过 [LINK]。这里是某人的学位论文，带有数据：[LINK]。还有像这样的有趣讨论 [LINK]：“根据我的经验，随着项目投入的时间和资源线性增长，TDD 的价值主张会呈指数级增长。”这也是我自己的经验。这个人的评论也很有趣，而且有数据 [LINK]。以上部分内容是实证（也就是科学的、不扯淡的）数据。我的看法已经发展到我认为 TDD 简直应该与编程不可分割，两者合在一起就应该直接叫“编程”。完全没有任何单元测试（无论是不是 TDD）应该被称为“为了省一点时间而冒愚蠢且极其危险的风险，就像开车时看手机”。至少 5 年来，我还没有发现哪个编程任务在通过 TDD 完成时不是写得好得多。有些事情，比如 IO，可能很难做单元测试，但这就是为什么我们有很好的思路来解决它，比如 Gary Bernhardt 那场精彩的《Boundaries》演讲 [VIDEO]
comments.text: Here is the infamous Nagappan TDD paper from Microsoft Research [LINK] Also discussed in this infoq article [LINK] Here's someone's thesis paper on it, with data: [LINK] There's also interesting discussions like this [LINK] "it is my experience that the value proposition for TDD grows exponentially as the time and resources involved in a project grows linearly." This has also been my own experience. This person's comment also is interesting and has data [LINK] Some of the above is empirical (read: scientific, no-bullshit) data. My opinion on it has grown to the point that I think TDD should literally be inseparable from programming, and the two together should simply be called, "programming." Lacking any unit tests whatsoever (TDD or otherwise) should be called, "taking stupid, extremely hazardous risks to save a little time, like reading your phone while driving" I've not found a programming task in at least 5 years that wasn't waaaay better-written when done via TDD. Some things, like IO, can be a challenge to unit-test, but that's why we have great ideas to solve that like Gary Bernhardt's awesome "Boundaries" talk [VIDEO]

comments.text: > I find some problems are solved better in an OO way such as interacting with a relational database. I've switched to functional interactions with a database, (Elixir/Ecto) and really, it's much better. In particular the explicit and declarative nature of the database interactions combines the convenience of an ORM with "not hiding important gotchas from you". I'm not arguing for pure functional systems (which I can see going very poorly with relational databases). There are some things that objects are good at like caching state as a model. But even here the FP systems typically do it better via FP actors and (again, impure) message passing, which enforces no-shared memory, and at least in erlang virtual machine systems, couples segregated state with limiting blast radius for your systems failure domains, which is 150% the "right thing to do". Of course if we're getting pedantic, this is even close to OO the way that Alan Kay imagined it, than what the OP and GP talk about, and I don't consider that to be OO in the contemporary, colloquial sense of "everything that happened after Bjarne Soustroup invented C++" I highly recommend this video for a more philosophical take on how to do "impure FP" without OO that is informed by a decade of industry experience: [VIDEO] which is by Gary Bernhardt (of WAT fame) > I look for the right tool for the job rather than some idealistic purity This is all about right tool for the job. IMO, FP code is easier to read, easier to reason about,

comments.text: A few years ago I was on a team and the dev lead had a practice of sharing Gary Bernhardt's Boundaries talk every time there was some degree of rotation or churn on the team. Almost part of the onboarding. As a functional programming aficionado, I didn't need the sales pitch, but it was the presentation that was gripping. Keep in mind, Ruby isn't a functional language, but here was this presenter describing essentially how you write good Haskell code, but in Ruby! A language that makes it so easy to mutate in place that it's known for libraries that "monkey patch" base classes and can change the definition of operators and functions at runtime! Fantastic talk, fantastic presentation. I now share it with my new engineering colleagues too. Here's the talk where he talks about imperative shell, functional core, "Boundaries": [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: 用于测试 UI 的命令式外壳、函数式内核思路。
comments.quote_zh: 我发现 Gary Bernhardt 的演讲《Boundaries》(1) 中的想法，对于弄清楚如何测试交互式 Web UI 非常有帮助。
comments.text_zh: 请原谅我表达得含糊且简短，但过去一年左右我一直在尝试测试我的 UI，这就是我得出的结论。我发现 Gary Bernhardt 的演讲《Boundaries》(1) 中的想法，对于弄清楚如何测试交互式 Web UI 非常有帮助。基本思路是，DOM 操作可以是一个“命令式外壳”，其中逻辑和条件分支尽可能少。用单独的函数和方法推导出 UI 组件的状态，这些函数和方法返回普通值（“函数式内核”），并为它们编写测试，因为针对值进行测试很容易。所以，不要测试类和 ID 是否存在。对你的命令式外壳测试一次，甚至可以手动测试或用集成测试测一次，这大概就够了。Angular 和 React 都鼓励类似的方法，但你并不需要这些技术才能这样做。例如在 Backbone 中，只要尽量避免在模板和 render 方法中出现条件和逻辑。如果你认为你的 UI 组件需要根据条件渲染，因为它可以处于不同状态，那就问问自己，这些状态是否只是外观上的差异，可以用类和 CSS 以声明式方式编程实现。此外，当你限制 API 表面积时，测试会容易得多。所以如果你使用的是像 Backbone 这样的库，其中模型和视图都有许多方法，并且有许多调用和使用它们的方式，那就不要让它们彼此直接引用。我曾在让模型和视图只通过一个 gl
comments.text: Forgive me for being vague and brief, but I've been trying to test my UIs for the last year or so and this is what I've come up with. I've found the ideas in Gary Bernhardt's talk, Boundaries (1), to be very helpful in figuring out how to test interactive web UIs. The basic idea is that DOM manipulation can be an "imperative shell" with as little logic and as few conditionals as possible. Derive the state of your UI component with separate functions and methods that return plain values (a "functional core"), and write tests for those because testing for values is easy. So no, don't test for the presence of classes and IDs. Test your imperative shell once, maybe even manually or with an integration test, and that's probably enough. Angular and React both encourage something like this approach, but you don't need those technologies to do it this way. In Backbone, for instance, just try to avoid conditionals and logic in your templates and render methods. If you think your UI piece needs to render with conditionals because it can be in different states, ask yourself if those states are just appearances that can be programmed declaratively with classes and CSS. Also, testing is so much easier when you limit API surface areas. So if you're using a library like Backbone, where models and views both have many methods with many ways they can be called and used, don't give them direct references to each other. comments.author: aszen
comments.why_zh: 关于函数式核心、命令式外壳的资源。
comments.quote_zh: 进一步探索这些理念的一些资源
comments.text_zh: 我一直在研究几种测试方法，到目前为止，以我的经验来看，是的，fakes 比 mocks 更好。但更好的是根本不需要 fake 或 mock 东西，尤其是在测试业务逻辑时。我们让自己陷入的问题之一，是把服务 IO 代码抽象成函数，然后从业务逻辑代码里调用它们。这迫使我们去 mock 所有 IO 调用；相反，我们应该做反过来的事，也就是把业务逻辑抽象成离散的、纯数据输入输出的函数，然后从我们的 IO 代码里调用这些函数。这样我们就能独立于 IO 代码来测试业务逻辑。现在测试业务逻辑变得相当简单，还可以利用 property testing 进一步增强我们对这类测试的信心。很多时候，剩下的 IO 代码只是在调用其他函数，并不需要测试。与此相关的其他一些理念还有 hexagonal architecture、Domain Driver Design、clean architecture，以及 functional core with an imperative shell。进一步探索这些理念的一些资源：Clean Architecture in Python - [LINK] Why integrated tests are a scam - [LINK] Boundaries - [VIDEO]
comments.text: I have been researching into several testing approaches and so far in my experience yes fakes are better than mocks. But what is even better is not having to fake or mock stuff especially for testing business logic. One of the problems we get ourselves into is abstracting service io code into functions and calling them from our business logic code. This forces us to mock all the io calls, instead we should be doing the opposite i.e abstracting business logic into discrete functions of pure data in and out and then calling those functions from our io code. This way we can test the business logic independently of the io code. Testing the business logic now becomes quite simple and one can leverage property testing to further boost our confidence in such tests. Many times the ramaining io code is just calling other functions and doesn't need to be tested. Several other ideas that relate to this are hexagonal architecture, Domain Driver Design, clean architecture and functional core with an imperative shell. Some resources to further explore these ideas: Clean Architecture in Python - [LINK] Why integrated tests are a scam - [LINK] Boundaries - [VIDEO]

comments.author: maxbond
comments.why_zh: 函数式核心、命令式外壳模式。
comments.quote_zh: 另见“函数式核心，命令式外壳”模式。
comments.text_zh: 你抓住要点了。通过把函数与应用状态解耦，你就能单独测试那个函数。比如，你可能会忍不住写一个函数：打开 HTTP 连接、执行 API 调用、解析结果并返回。但测试这个函数会非常困难。如果你把它拆成几个小函数（一个打开连接，一个接收已打开的连接并执行调用，一个解析结果），测试起来就会容易得多。（这是我按前面说的方式写代码、给它写测试、后来又发现好几个 bug 时顿悟的。我意识到我的测试什么都没做，也没抓住 bug，因为我写的代码根本没法测试。一般来说，副作用和全局状态是测试性的敌人。）最后你会得到接收很多参数（10 个以上）的函数，一开始会觉得不对劲，但这是值得的，而且 IDE 能帮上大忙。这个模式叫依赖注入。[链接] 另见“函数式核心，命令式外壳”模式。[视频]
comments.text: You've got the gist of it. By decoupling your function from the state of your application, you can test that function in isolation. For instance, you might be tempted to write a function that opens an HTTP connection, performs an API call, parses the result, and returns it. But you'll have a really hard time testing that function. If you decompose it into several tiny functions (one that opens a connection, one that accepts an open connection and performs the call, and one that parses the result), you'll have a much easier time testing it. (This clicked for me when I wrote code as I've described, wrote tests for it, and later found several bugs. I realized my tests did nothing and failed to catch my bugs, because the code I'd written was impossible to test. In general, side effects and global state are the enemies of testability.) You end up with functions that take a lot of arguments (10+), which can feel wrong at first, but it's worth it, and IDEs help enormously. This pattern is called dependency injection. [LINK] See also, the "functional core, imperative shell" pattern. [VIDEO]
